## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The PR regenerates `aaa-generated/catalog.json`, which renames all 1,500 `legacy-service-NNNN` entries to `production-service-NNNN` and moves their ports from 10xxx to 20xxx. It also rewrites `healthy()` in `services/registry.py` as `not failures`, which behaves the same for lists, and changes the release approval check in `zzz-release/gate.py`. The approval change adds an off-by-one error: a release with exactly the minimum number of approvals is now blocked, so this should not merge until it is fixed.

## Critical
- zzz-release/gate.py:5 — correctness — `approved` changed from `approvals >= minimum` to `approvals > minimum`, so `approved(2, minimum=2)` now returns `False`. This contradicts the module docstring at line 1: "A release needs at least the configured number of approvals." The tests in `tests/test_release.py:11-16` only use 3 and 1 approvals, never the boundary value, so they still pass. — Every release with exactly the required number of approvals (2 by default) is wrongly blocked, and the test suite does not catch it.

## Important
(none)

## Suggestions
(none)

## Strengths
- `tests/test_release.py:19-21` covers both the empty and non-empty failure lists for the rewritten `healthy()`, which confirms the new version matches the old one for list inputs.
- The catalog regeneration is uniform: every renamed entry keeps `"enabled": true`, and each one's port offset matches its new service index.

## Not reviewed
- No catalog generator or source config is in the repository, so I could not check whether the regenerated `aaa-generated/catalog.json` matches what the generator would actually produce.
- Nothing in the repository reads `aaa-generated/catalog.json`, so I could not check how the renamed services and new ports affect deployment.
